title: Redirect rule item (erMatchRule)
$comment: The DynamoDB item shape the Lambda@Edge reads for a redirect (viewer-request). Modeled on EdgeRedirectRule/MatchCondition from the source project's redirect-rule-types.ts.

pk.description: Host, e.g. www.example.com. DynamoDB partition key.

sk.description: REDIRECT#<priority>, priority zero-padded to 5 digits; lower = higher priority; unique per host per type.

disabled.$comment: Optional; absent means enabled. The Lambda@Edge filters out rules where disabled=true (RulesService.loadRules), so a toggle takes effect within the edge cache TTL (~1 min). The console writes it through PATCH.

match.$comment: Shared match condition, referenced by rewrite-rule.schema.json. Field names/enums mirror MatchCondition + MatchType/MatchOperator in redirect-rule-types.ts.

headerName.description: Required when matchType is "header"; disallowed otherwise.

cookieName.description: Required when matchType is "cookie"; disallowed otherwise. The name alone, never "name=value".
cookieName.$comment: RFC 6265 forbids separators in a cookie name, so `=`, `;`, `,` and whitespace cannot appear in one. The pattern is here for a second reason: a `Cookie` header reads `locale=nl`, so someone filling in a field labelled "cookie name" will paste the whole pair. Stored, that name matches nothing a viewer ever sends, and the rule silently never fires — the same class of failure the field was added to remove.

allOf.$comment: headerName is required iff matchType is "header".

A cookie condition names the cookie it tests, exactly as a header condition names the header. Without it the only thing the edge can compare against is the whole `Cookie` header — one line holding every cookie — so `equals` can never be true and `contains` matches unrelated cookies. `required` on matchType so an item missing it fails on that alone, without a second error about a field its type may not even take.
